questions.question:
How many of the following compounds will have POS (Plane of symmetry) :
$ $(i) (ii)
$ $(iii) (iv)
$ $(v) (vi)
$ $(vii) (viii)
$ $
questions.explanation:
**Question Explanation:
$ The$ question asks to **determine the total number of given structures that possess at least one plane of symmetry (POS).

$ $ **Concept:
$ A$ **plane of symmetry (POS) is an imaginary plane that divides a molecule into **two identical mirror-image halves. The presence or absence of POS depends on molecular geometry and the spatial arrangement of substituents.

$ $ **Solution:

$ $ (i) **Substituted allene:
$ Chiral$ allenes having different groups (e.g., Cl and H) on each terminal carbon are **asymmetric and hence **do not possess a POS.

$ $ (ii) **Trans-1,3-dichlorocyclobutane:
$ Has$ a **vertical plane of symmetry passing through C-1 and C-3.
$ \u$2714 **POS present

$ $ (iii) **Norbornane (bridged bicyclic system):
$ Highly$ symmetrical structure with **multiple planes of symmetry.
$ \u$2714 **POS present

$ $ (iv) **Trans-1,3-dimethylcyclopentane:
$ Asymmetric$ due to substituent arrangement; unlike the cis-isomer, it **lacks a POS.

$ $ (v) **Cis-1,2-dimethylcyclopropane:
$ Different$ spatial orientation of substituents destroys symmetry.
$ \u$2718 **No POS

$ $ (vi) **Cyclohexane (chair conformation):
$ A$ highly symmetrical structure possessing **several planes of symmetry.
$ \u$2714 **POS present

$ $ (vii) **1,3,5-substituted cyclohexane:
$ A$ symmetrical arrangement (Br vs Br), giving a **plane of symmetry.
$ \u$2714 **POS present

$ $ (viii) **Asymmetrically substituted cyclohexane (Br and Cl):
$ Different$ substituents break symmetry.
$ \u$2718 **No POS

$ $ Thus, compounds **(ii), (iii), (vi), and (vii) possess at least one plane of symmetry.

$ $ **Final Answer: **4

$ $
